title: WPSS/2637/2015 of Jyoti AND OTHERS Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/S) No. 2637 of 2015
Jyoti & others Ö Petitioners
Vs
State of Uttarakhand & others Ö Respondents
With
Writ Petition (S/S) No. 2636 of 2015
Km. Savita & others Ö Petitioners
Vs
State of Uttarakhand & others Ö Respondents
With
Writ Petition (S/S) No. 2640 of 2015
Km. Manisha Semwal & others Ö Petitioners
Vs
State of Uttarakhand & others Ö Respondents
None present for the petitioners.
Ms. Prabha Naithani, Brief Holder, present for the State of Uttarakhand.
Mr. Tarun Lakhera, Advocate, present for private respondents.
Honíble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J. (Oral)
1. The petitioners are the teachers working as a Guest
Teacher in various Government Schools in the State of
Uttarakhand. The appointment of such teachers has been
done by the State Government to meet the contingency which
has arisen in the Government schools, due to vacancy of
teachers.
2. Learned counsel for the private respondent submits
that the similar controversy has already been decided by this
Court vide order dated 10.08.2016 passed in WPSS No. 1093 of
2016 (Alok Parmar & others Vs State of Uttarakhand & others).
3. The matter related to the Guest Teacher has come
up before this Court earlier in WPSS No. 1093 of 2016 wherein
this Court has already held that the entire scheme of ìGuest
Teacherî is violative of Article 14 of the Constitution of India
and the scheme of Guest Teacher was declared

2
unconstitutional. Since this was brought to the notice of this
Court that there are certain remote areas where posts of
Assistant Teachers are lying vacant, which cannot be filled
immediately, therefore, purely as a last resort measure, it was
directed that in such blocks, where competent and fully eligible
Assistant Teachers having all qualifications, including
Teachers Eligibility Test, are available, they may continue as a
stop-gap arrangement till regular incumbents are selected and
formally joins the post, but not beyond 31.03.2017. Such relief
was granted purely in the interest of students.
4. In view thereof, the present writ petitions stand
disposed in the same terms and conditions as made in the
WPSS No. 1093 of 2016 (Alok Parman & others Vs State of
Uttarakhand & others decided on 10.08.2016). Interim orders
23.12.2015 passed in the present matters stand vacated.
